properties.chose: Options (a) and (c), on Anthony's word 2026-10-12 ("agree with your recommendations for speeding up passing CI and merging PRs"): for a small change the local run covers only the checks the change touches, in a worktree whose build is already warm, and CI runs the whole gate set once before the merge. (b), making the local run the gate, is declined, because a local subset read as the whole is the measured hazard. (d), retiring the per-PR design ritual, is the accepted nightly-check requirement, now marked high priority. The measurement behind it: a cold worktree spent 35m 22s compiling for 0.79 s of tests.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-12: "I feel like we run everything locally and then run CI checks on top of it. The end result is that it takes like ~1 hour or more to get a simple change small change like rewording of a skill to be merged."

WHAT THE HOUR WAS MADE OF ON 2026-10-12, as observed in the session (not timed step by step): a new worktree per change, whose first cargo build compiles RocksDB from cold (the project's own rule puts that at about 34 minutes, rule:never-a-bare-cargo-clean-on-the-dev-box); local tests; the design hold, record and copy for the PR; then CI's long job of 16–25 minutes; then waiting for the owner's named merge.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) CI is the gate. Locally, run only what the change touches (for a skill rewording: the skill lint and its suite, the init suite, the findability test), push, and let CI run everything once. Cost: a CI failure costs another push and another CI run.
(b) The local run is the gate and CI is advisory for small changes. Cost: a local run is not independent and leaves no shared record; this project's CI exists partly because local runs were subsets read as the whole.
(c) Keep both, but stop paying the cold build locally: reuse one worktree per line of work, or a compiler cache shared across worktrees (safe, unlike a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, which built another branch's code).
(d) Remove the per-PR design ritual instead: req:a-nightly-check-on-the-box-runs-reflow2s-client-against-the-hosted-design-and-the-copy-retires is ACCEPTED intent, not yet built, and retires the hold, the per-PR copy and its gate. That is a different lever on the same hour, and it is already decided, not an idea.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT to (a) and (b), on the record: running a subset of the gate set and reading it as the whole happened four times in one day (fact:a-local-feature-error-was-worked-around-instead-of-read-as-the-ci-contract). (a) is safe only because CI still runs everything before a merge; (b) gives that up.

WHICH IS CHEAPER: (a) and (c) need no code, only a change in how the work is done; (d) is real work already decided; (b) is cheap in minutes and expensive in assurance. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

MEASURED 2026-10-12 while this was being recorded: the local findability test for the capture-session rewording (a five-line text change) ran in a fresh worktree, and its first cargo build had been in RocksDB's C++ compile (four compiler processes, no log line) for 25 minutes before a single test ran. The cost options (c) and dec:idea-ci-tests-on-the-in-memory-backend-unless-the-store-changes aim at was being paid on a change that touches no store code. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

RESULT of that run: the build finished in 35m 22s and the four skill-findability tests then passed in 0.79 s. For this change, 99.96% of the local wait was compiling, most of it RocksDB's C++ in a cold worktree, and 0.04% was testing. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-12 — a small change runs the full gate set once, in CI; locally only the checks it touches, in a worktree whose build is already warm
properties.rationale: Recorded open with its counter-argument. The owner's hour is the measure; no option was timed.
